numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With method='linear' on a 2D grid of single points (points=([0],[0])) and float64 values, calling the interpolator returns NaN at the grid point. The same setup with float32 values returns 0.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The interpolator should return the grid value at the single grid point, array([0.]), as the float32 case already does. The fix removed the branch in evaluate_linear_2d that set out[point] = NAN.
trigger_conditions: 2D grid (ndim=2) where every axis has length 1, e.g. points=([0],[0])
evaluated at the grid point, e.g. rgi([[0,0]])

category_specific_evidence: Bug is a single-point (length-one axes) degenerate grid case in RegularGridInterpolator with method linear returning NaN instead of the grid value
Reproducer: points=([0],[0]), values=np.array([[0]], dtype=np.float32), method='linear', calling rgi([[0,0]]) returns array([0.]) per issue #23171
Commit message: test_length_one_axes fails for parametrization test_length_one_axes[linear-2-float64] as of commit 4c1a4da81, but is OK in all other cases
PR #23253 states that in the specific case of a 2D, float64 grid a NaN is returned for linear interpolation on a single-point grid
Cython fix in _rgi_cython.pyx adds a branch returning values[0, 0] when grid[0] and grid[1] both have length 1, and removes the out[point] = NAN branches for non-finite inputs
Test values: val = 1/7 at a single grid point, fill value 1/42 used when bounds_error=False
Expected value at the single grid point is the stored value itself (no interpolation is possible)
reproduction_risks: Exact expected values are not fully given in the passages beyond the reproducer output of 0.; test value 1/7 is in the test design but the expected output for test_length_one_axis_all is truncated
Discussion of test refactoring (np.asarray([0]*ndim) vs arange) means test coordinates are not settled in the passages
The removed NaN branches mean out-of-bounds/NaN inputs now rely on caller handling; reproduction should not assume NaN output
